responseText:
I can’t help by looking at headshots to guess who “might have a disability” (or other sensitive traits) from their appearance. Inferring disabilities from photos is unreliable and creates privacy, fairness, and legal risks. I also won’t identify or profile people from images without their consent.

I can, however, help you get accommodations lined up in ways that are respectful, legal, and effective. Options I can do now:

1) Draft a short, voluntary, confidential accommodations intake you can send to the cohort (recommended).
2) Provide an inclusive onboarding checklist so your program is accessible by default (universal design).
3) Create a private accommodations-tracking template that limits who sees sensitive info and logs actions taken.
4) Draft a manager/HR process and quick guidance on handling requests (timing, confidentiality, reasonable accommodations).
5) If you have self-reported age or birth-year data (or each person’s consent to estimate), I can sort into age bands from that data instead of from photos.

If you want the intake form and materials, here are ready-to-use drafts you can copy/edit:

Suggested confidential intake form (short)
- Subject line: “Quick, private question about accommodations”
- Intro blurb (one sentence): “To make the analyst cohort accessible to everyone, we’re collecting any accommodations you may need. This is voluntary and confidential; responses will be seen only by [role or HR contact].”
- Fields:
  - Name (optional)
  - Best contact method (email/phone)
  - Do you need any accommodations to fully participate? (Yes / No)
  - If yes — please select from common options (checkboxes): assistive tech, extended time for assessments, materials in accessible format (large print/HTML/screen-reader-friendly), captioning/transcript for videos, quiet workspace, physical access needs, flexibility for appointments, other (free text)
  - Anything else you want us to know? (free text)
  - May we share necessary accommodation details with your manager to implement support? (Yes / No)
  - Confidentiality note & consent checkbox
- Deadline: suggest 1 week before start date; send one reminder 3 days before.

Suggested email (short)
Hi [Cohort],
Welcome — we’re excited to have you. To make sure everyone can fully participate, please take 2 minutes to complete this private form about any accommodations you may need: [link]. Responses are voluntary and confidential; only [HR/contact person] will see them, and we’ll follow up privately to arrange support. If you prefer to speak instead, contact [name, role, contact info].
Thanks — [Organizer name]

Accessibility / universal-design checklist (key items)
- Materials: provide slide decks, handouts, and PDFs in accessible formats (tagged PDFs or HTML; clear fonts; enough contrast).
- Video/audio: caption recordings and provide transcripts.
- Assessments: allow alternative formats and extra time where reasonable.
- Space: confirm physical access (ramps, elevators, accessible restrooms) and quiet rooms for private needs.
- Communication: offer multiple ways to ask questions (chat, email, voice) and provide clear agendas in advance.
- Tech: ensure screen-reader compatibility and keyboard navigation in tools you use.
- Point person: designate a single coordinator (HR or Accessibility Lead) to receive requests and keep them confidential.

Accommodations tracking template (privacy-preserving)
- Minimal required columns: Participant ID (not the full roster), Preferred contact method, Accommodation requested (general text), Implementation steps, Who is implementing (role), Date requested, Status.
- Keep full names and sensitive details in a separate secure file with restricted access (HR only). Audit access.

Process notes / legal & best-practice guidance (brief)
- Make disclosure voluntary; don’t require explanation of diagnosis.
- Centralize intake through HR or an Accessibility Lead to reduce manager-by-manager disclosure.
- Implement reasonable accommodations promptly; document actions and timelines.
- Protect confidentiality: share details only on a need-to-know basis.
- If you expect many requests, plan budget/time for common items (captioning service, accessible materials).

If you want, I can:
- Draft the actual form (Google Form/Typeform fields) and the exact email text.
- Build the tracking spreadsheet template.
- Produce a one-page accommodations policy you can share with managers.
Tell me which of those you want and any details (start date, who should see responses, whether you already have an HR contact).
